points.description: Core fact: set a pointer to the first element of the array (the array name/base address), then add the index/offset to the pointer to reach an element (e.g. *(p + i) or *(arr + i)).
points.partial_credit: Award about 2-3 marks if only one half is given: either the pointer points to the array's start/first element, or an offset/index is added to a pointer, without linking the two.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying, in any wording, that a pointer is made to point at the array's first element and the index (offset) is added to it to reach an element; examples like *(p+i) are fine. Part marks if only the pointer-to-first-element idea or only the add-offset idea is given. No marks for unrelated descriptions such as ordinary arr[i] subscripting with no pointer or offset. Extra correct detail or minor wrong remarks do not cost marks.
